title: AT&T Expands Fiber to 12 New Metro Areas: What It Means for Your Bill
html:
AT&T announced this week that its fiber internet service is rolling out to twelve additional metropolitan areas, part of a broader push to reach 30 million locations by the end of next year. The expansion targets mid-sized cities that have historically been served only by slower cable or DSL connections.

For households in the newly covered areas, the practical upshot is competition. Where AT&T fiber arrives, local cable providers have historically responded with promotional pricing, so it is worth checking whether your current provider will match new-customer rates even if you don't switch.

The plans start at symmetrical speeds, meaning upload and download are equal — a meaningful difference for anyone who works from home, video calls frequently, or uploads large files. That said, the headline promotional price typically rises after the first 12 months, so read the fine print before committing.

If fiber isn't yet at your address, AT&T's coverage checker is the fastest way to confirm, and it's worth re-checking quarterly as the buildout continues.
meta_description: AT&T fiber reaches 12 new metro areas. Here's what the expansion means for pricing, speeds, and your options.
